Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

shield noun

also shields, toy shield

classical

Liv. 21.28.1
Tac. Germ. 6
Caes. BG 2.21 (Lewis & Short)

scūtum, scūtī n.

noun, second declension

shield (the long, oblong kind)

The legionary’s shield, of boards covered with leather (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • clipeus (clupeus), clipeī m. — a round shield

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.97 (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 2.443 (Lewis & Short)

    The round bronze shield; also neuter, clipeum (Lewis & Short).

  • parma, parmae f. — a small round shield

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Liv. 2.20 (Lewis & Short); Hor. C. 2.7.10: relictā nōn bene parmulā

    Carried by the light infantry and the cavalry; in the poets any shield (Lewis & Short). The diminutive is parmula.

Examples

  • Gallī occursant in rīpā cum variīs ululātibus cantūque mōris suī, quatientēs scūta super capita

    the Gauls came running to meet them on the bank with all kinds of howls and songs in their fashion, shaking their shields above their headsLiv. 21.28.1

  • Scūtum relīquisse praecipuum flāgitium

    to have left one’s shield behind is the greatest disgraceTac. Germ. 6

  • Scūtō circumdabit tē vēritās ejus

    his truth will surround you like a shieldVulg. Ps. 90 (91), 5

See also sword, weapon, helmet, protect.
